acceptance: Spark adapters pick toArrow, Arrow-enabled toPandas, or collect() by runtime version; unit tests with stubbed DataFrames cover each of the three paths and the version switch, and live pyspark 3.5 and 4.x runs are recorded where those environments exist (a missing environment is named, not skipped silently).
context:
2026-11-03: the fetch-timing contract is decided in fetch-timing-contract-decision-20261103 and implemented by perf-arrow-aware-result-capture-20261030. Under the recommended option, full Arrow receipt (including draining streaming readers) stays inside the query timer and fetch_mode is recorded; Arrow-to-rows conversion for digests stays outside it. Re-read the recorded decision before starting; if the owner chose differently, update this item's acceptance. Origin: root-cause analysis of RF1 timing and its adversarial review.

Guardrails (added 2026-11-03): no live-cloud runs (Databricks, Athena, BigQuery, Snowflake, ClickHouse Cloud, MotherDuck) without owner approval quoted in context; an adapter without a passing digest-parity run keeps rows as its default fetch; heavy runs only through make heavy-run or a lock-taking entry point; no explanatory comments in source (make comment-policy-check); changelog.d fragment required; re-read cited symbols before editing, since line numbers drift.
description: base/spark_execution_mixin.py:372 uses collect(), building Python Row objects. DataFrame.toArrow exists only in pyspark 4.0+; pyproject allows pyspark>=3.5.0 and databricks-connect 16.1.7 (locked for Python <3.12) is Spark 3.5-based. Use toArrow when available, else toPandas with spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled, else collect(). Covers spark, pyspark, lakesail, velox, EMR/Glue/Dataproc/Fabric/Synapse Spark. snowpark_connect.py:285 is a Snowpark DataFrame (not PySpark): Snowpark 1.48 has DataFrame.to_arrow, but check whether it hits the same pandas<3 gate as the Snowflake connector.
